title.zh: 卷六十九 竇何列傳
title.raw: 卷六十九 竇何列傳 Volume 69: Biographies of Dou, He

sentences.zh: 竇武字游平，扶風平陵人，安豐戴侯融之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Dou Wu, courtesy name Youping, was a native of Pingling in Fufeng, and was the great-great-grandson of the Marquis Dai of Anfeng, Dou Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu, styled Youping, came from Pingling in Fufeng; he was a fourth-generation descendant of Dou Rong, Marquis Dai of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 父奉，定襄太守。

translations.literal: His father was Dou Feng, governor of Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dou Feng had served as governor of Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 武少以經行著稱，常教授於大澤中，不交時事，名顯關西。

translations.literal: In youth Wu was renowned for his classical learning and conduct; he often taught in great marshlands, did not involve himself in current affairs, and his name was illustrious west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: From his youth Dou Wu was known for scholarship and upright conduct; he taught students amid the wetlands, kept clear of politics, and his reputation spread through the Guanxi region.

sentences.zh: 延熹八年，長女選入掖庭，桓帝以為貴人，拜武郎中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yanxi, his eldest daughter was selected and entered the Rear Palace; Emperor Huan made her an honored lady and appointed Wu gentleman of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 165 CE his eldest daughter was chosen for the imperial harem; Emperor Huan elevated her to honored consort and named Dou Wu a gentleman attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 其冬，貴人立為皇后，武遷越騎校尉，封槐里侯，五千戶。

translations.literal: That winter the honored lady was established as empress; Wu was promoted colonel of the agile cavalry, enfeoffed marquis of Huaili with five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: That same winter she became empress; Dou Wu rose to colonel of the swift cavalry and received the title Marquis of Huaili with a fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，拜城門校尉。

translations.literal: The next winter he was appointed colonel of the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he was named colonel of the city gates.

sentences.zh: 在位多辟名士，清身疾惡，禮賂不通，妻子衣食裁充足而已。

translations.literal: In office he often summoned famous scholars, purified himself and hated evil, did not communicate through ritual bribes, and his wife and children had clothing and food only just sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: In office he recruited eminent scholars, kept himself scrupulously clean and detested corruption, refused illicit gifts, and saw to it that his family had only what they needed.

sentences.zh: 是時羌蠻寇難，歲儉民飢，武得兩宮賞賜，悉散與太學諸生，及載肴糧於路，飩施貧民。

translations.literal: At that time the Qiang and Man brought calamity, the year was lean and the people hungry; Wu obtained rewards from the two palaces, all scattered them to the students of the Imperial Academy, and moreover loaded viands and grain on the roads and fed the poor.
translations.idiomatic: With Qiang and southern tribes raiding and famine stalking the land, Dou Wu took every gift from the two palaces and gave it to the Imperial Academy students, and he had food carted along the roads to feed the destitute.

sentences.zh: 兄子紹，為虎賁中郎將，性疏簡奢侈。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Shao was a leader of the palace tiger guard, by nature careless, simple, and extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Dou Shao commanded the palace tiger guard; he was careless by temperament and lived lavishly.

sentences.zh: 武每數切厲相戒，猶不覺悟，乃上書求退紹位，又自責不能訓導，當先受罪。

translations.literal: Wu repeatedly sternly admonished him, yet he still did not awaken; then he submitted a memorial requesting to remove Shao from office, and moreover blamed himself for being unable to instruct and guide, saying he should first receive punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu remonstrated with him sharply time and again, but the young man did not reform; Dou Wu then memorialized asking that Shao be dismissed and declared himself unfit as a mentor, offering to accept punishment first.

sentences.zh: 由是紹更遵節，大小莫敢違犯。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shao further observed restraint, and great and small none dared violate him.
translations.idiomatic: After that Dou Shao minded his conduct, and everyone in the household obeyed without exception.

sentences.zh: 時國政多失，內官專寵，李膺、杜密等為黨事考逮。

translations.literal: At that time state policy had many errors, inner officials monopolized favor, and Li Ying, Du Mi, and others were examined and arrested on account of the partisan affair.
translations.idiomatic: The government was adrift, eunuchs held unchecked favor, and men such as Li Ying and Du Mi were rounded up in the partisan prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 永康元年，上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, he submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In 167 CE he presented a memorial of remonstrance that began:

sentences.zh: 書奏，因以病上還城門校尉、槐里侯印綬。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, on account of illness he submitted and returned the seals of colonel of the city gates and marquis of Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting it, he cited illness and tendered the seals of his posts as colonel of the city gates and Marquis of Huaili.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，有詔原李膺、杜密等，自黃門北寺、若盧、都內諸獄，繫囚罪輕者皆出之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it; there was an edict pardoning Li Ying, Du Mi, and others; from the Yellow Gate North Prison, Ruolu, and the various prisons of the capital, all bound prisoners whose crimes were light were released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused his resignation and issued an edict pardoning Li Ying, Du Mi, and their associates; minor offenders were freed from the eunuch-run North Prison, Ruolu, and the metropolitan jails.

sentences.zh: 其冬帝崩，無嗣。

translations.literal: That winter the emperor died; there was no heir.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Emperor Huan died without a son to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 武召侍御史河閒劉儵，參問其國中王子侯之賢者，儵稱解瀆亭侯宏。

translations.literal: Wu summoned attendant censor Liu Shu of Hejian, consulted him on worthy princes and marquises in that state, and Shu praised Marquis Hong of the Jiedu pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu called in the attendant censor Liu Shu of Hejian and asked which of the imperial clansmen there was fit to rule; Liu Shu recommended Liu Hong, Marquis of the Jiedu pavilion.

sentences.zh: 武入白太后，遂徵立之，是為靈帝。

translations.literal: Wu entered and reported to the empress dowager; then (Hong) was summoned and established; this was Emperor Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu laid the matter before the empress dowager; Liu Hong was summoned and enthroned as Emperor Ling.

sentences.zh: 拜武為大將軍，常居禁中。

translations.literal: Wu was appointed grand general and constantly resided within the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu was named grand general and took up permanent residence inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝既立，論定策功，更封武為聞喜侯；

translations.literal: When the emperor had been established, they assessed merit in settling the succession, and Wu was further enfeoffed marquis of Wenxi;
translations.idiomatic: Once the new emperor was enthroned, those who had settled the succession were rewarded, and Dou Wu received a further enfeoffment as Marquis of Wenxi;

sentences.zh: 子機渭陽侯，拜侍中；

translations.literal: his son Ji was marquis of Weiyang, appointed palace attendant;
translations.idiomatic: his son Dou Ji became Marquis of Weiyang and a palace attendant;

sentences.zh: 兄子紹鄠侯，遷步兵校尉；

translations.literal: his elder brother's son Shao was marquis of Hu, promoted colonel of foot soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: his nephew Dou Shao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hu and promoted to colonel of the footsoldiers;

sentences.zh: 紹弟靖西鄉侯，為侍中，監羽林左騎。

translations.literal: Shao's younger brother Jing was marquis of Xixiang, was palace attendant, and supervised the left wing of the feathered forest.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Shao's younger brother Dou Jing was made Marquis of Xixiang, served as palace attendant, and oversaw the left wing of the Feathered Forest guard.

sentences.zh: 武既輔朝政，常有誅翦宦官之意，太傅陳蕃亦素有謀。

translations.literal: When Wu had assisted court government, he constantly had the intention to execute and extirpate the eunuchs; the grand tutor Chen Fan also long had plans.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister Dou Wu meant to purge the eunuchs, and Grand Tutor Chen Fan had long nursed the same design.

sentences.zh: 時共會朝堂，蕃私謂武曰：「中常侍曹節、王甫等，自先帝時操弄國權，濁亂海內，百姓匈匈，歸咎於此。

translations.literal: At the time they jointly met in the court hall; Fan privately said to Wu: "The palace attendants Cao Jie, Wang Fu, and others, since the former emperor's time have grasped and played with state power, defiled and thrown into disorder the realm within the seas; the hundred surnames are in an uproar and ascribe blame to this.
translations.idiomatic: When they met at court, Chen Fan took Dou Wu aside and said, "Cao Jie, Wang Fu, and their fellow eunuchs have twisted the levers of power since the previous reign; the empire is in turmoil and the people lay every ill at their door.

sentences.zh: 今不誅節等，後必難圖。

translations.literal: If now we do not execute Jie and the others, later it will certainly be difficult to plan.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not cut them down now, we will never manage it later."

sentences.zh: 」武深然之。

translations.literal: " Wu deeply approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 蕃大喜，以手推席而起。

translations.literal: Fan was greatly pleased; with his hand he pushed the mat and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan was elated; he pushed himself up from his seat.

sentences.zh: 武於是引同志尹勳為尚書令，劉瑜為侍中，馮述為屯騎校尉；

translations.literal: Thereupon Wu brought in like-minded Yin Xun as director of the secretariat, Liu Yu as palace attendant, Feng Shu as colonel of garrison cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu then appointed allies to key posts: Yin Xun as director of the secretariat, Liu Yu as palace attendant, and Feng Shu as colonel of garrison cavalry;

sentences.zh: 又徵天下名士廢黜者前司隸李膺、宗正劉猛、太僕杜密、廬江太守朱宇等，列於朝廷；

translations.literal: and further summoned to the court famous scholars of the realm who had been dismissed: former metropolitan commandant Li Ying, director of the imperial clan Liu Meng, grand coachman Du Mi, governor of Lujiang Zhu Yu, and others, arraying them at court;
translations.idiomatic: he recalled celebrated men who had been cashiered—among them the former metropolitan commandant Li Ying, the director of the imperial clan Liu Meng, the grand coachman Du Mi, and the governor of Lujiang Zhu Yu—and seated them again at court;

sentences.zh: 請前越巂太守荀翌為從事中郎，辟潁川陳寔為屬：共定計策。

translations.literal: requested the former governor of Yuegui Xun Yi as staff supervisor, summoned Chen Shi of Yingchuan as subordinate: together they settled plans and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: he named the former governor of Yuegui, Xun Yi, as staff supervisor and recruited Chen Shi of Yingchuan as an aide, and with them he hammered out a strategy.

sentences.zh: 於是天下雄俊，知其風旨，莫不延頸企踵，思奮其智力。

translations.literal: Thereupon the heroes and outstanding men of the realm, knowing their intent, none did not crane their necks and stand on tiptoe, thinking to exert their intelligence and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Word of their purpose spread, and bold men across the empire strained to join them, eager to lend mind and muscle to the cause.

sentences.zh: 會五月日食，蕃復說武曰：「昔蕭望之困一石顯，近者李、杜諸公禍及妻子，況今石顯數十輩乎！

translations.literal: It happened that in the fifth month there was a solar eclipse; Fan again persuaded Wu, saying: "In the past Xiao Wangzhi was trapped by a single Shi Xian; in recent times the misfortune of the various gentlemen Li and Du reached their wives and children; how much more now are there several tens of generations of Shi Xian!
translations.idiomatic: A solar eclipse in the fifth month gave Chen Fan his opening. He urged Dou Wu: "Xiao Wangzhi fell to one Shi Xian; Li Ying, Du Mi, and their circle lost even their families—and today we face dozens of Shi Xians.

sentences.zh: 蕃以八十之年，欲為將軍除害，今可且因日食，斥罷宦官，以塞天變。

translations.literal: Fan, at the age of eighty years, wishes for the general to remove the harm; now we can temporarily because of the solar eclipse dismiss and remove the eunuchs, in order to block heaven's mutation.
translations.idiomatic: I am eighty, yet I mean to help you root out this evil; use the eclipse as heaven's warning and sweep the eunuchs from office to answer the portent."

sentences.zh: 又趙夫人及女尚書，旦夕亂太后，急宜退絕。

translations.literal: Moreover Lady Zhao and the female secretaries morning and evening throw the empress dowager into disorder; urgently they should be retired and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhao and the women secretaries who haunt the empress dowager day and night must be removed at once."

sentences.zh: 惟將軍慮焉。

translations.literal: Only the general should consider this.
translations.idiomatic: General, this rests with you."

sentences.zh: 」武乃白太后曰：「故事，黃門、常侍但當給事省內，典門戶，主近署財物耳。

translations.literal: " Wu then reported to the empress dowager, saying: "According to precedent, yellow gates and regular palace attendants ought only to supply service within the palace, manage doors and gates, and preside over the finances of nearby offices.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu laid the case before the empress dowager: "By established practice, eunuchs of the Yellow Gate and regular attendants should stick to palace service—guarding doors and handling petty accounts."

sentences.zh: 今乃使與政事而任權重，子弟布列，專為貪暴。

translations.literal: Now they are made to participate in government affairs and are entrusted with heavy power; sons and younger brothers are spread in array, exclusively practicing greed and violence.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they dabble in state affairs and wield real power; their kinsmen fill every office and grow rich by extortion."

sentences.zh: 天下匈匈，正以此故。

translations.literal: The realm within the seas is in an uproar; it is precisely because of this reason.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the realm is in an uproar."

sentences.zh: 宜悉誅廢，以清朝廷。

translations.literal: It is fitting entirely to execute and abolish them, in order to purify the court.
translations.idiomatic: They ought to be purged wholesale so the court can be cleansed."

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「漢來故事世有，但當誅其有罪，豈可盡廢邪？

translations.literal: " The empress dowager said: "Since Han, precedent has existed in every generation; one ought only to execute those who have crimes; how can one entirely abolish them?
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager replied, "Han has always used eunuchs at court; execute the guilty if you must, but you cannot abolish the institution root and branch."

sentences.zh: 」時中常侍管霸頗有才略，專制省內。

translations.literal: " At that time the regular palace attendant Guan Ba had considerable talent and strategy and monopolized control within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Guan Ba was clever and ruthless and dominated the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 武先白誅霸及中常侍蘇康等，竟死。

translations.literal: Wu first reported and executed Ba and the regular palace attendant Su Kang and others; in the end they died.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu obtained permission to execute Guan Ba, Su Kang, and their clique, and they were put to death.

sentences.zh: 武復數白誅曹節等，太后冘豫未忍，故事久不發。

translations.literal: Wu again several times reported to execute Cao Jie and others; the empress dowager hesitated and could not bear it, therefore the affair long did not break out.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Wu repeatedly asked leave to move against Cao Jie, the empress dowager wavered, and the great purge never came.

sentences.zh: 至八月，太白出西方。

translations.literal: When it reached the eighth month, the Great White appeared in the west.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Venus blazed in the western sky.

sentences.zh: 劉瑜素善天官，惡之，上書皇太后曰：「太白犯房左驂，上將星入太微，其占宮門當閉，將相不利，姦人在主傍。

translations.literal: Liu Yu was always good at celestial offices; he hated it and submitted a memorial to the empress dowager, saying: "The Great White encroaches on the left side-horse of the chamber; the upper general star enters the supreme enclosure; its omen is that the palace gates ought to close, generals and ministers are unlucky, and evil men are beside the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, who was versed in astrology, took it as a dire sign and wrote the empress dowager: "Venus has struck the left rein-star of the House constellation; the commander star has entered the Purple Palace—an omen of sealed palace gates, peril for ministers and generals, and villains at the ruler's elbow.

sentences.zh: 願急防之。

translations.literal: I wish urgently to guard against it.
translations.idiomatic: You must act before it is too late."

sentences.zh: 」又與武、蕃書，以星辰錯繆，不利大臣，宜速斷大計。

translations.literal: " He also wrote a letter to Wu and Fan, because the stars and constellations were in disorder, unlucky for great ministers; it was fitting speedily to decide the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a separate letter to Dou Wu and Chen Fan: the heavens were out of joint—a bad sign for high ministers—and they should strike without delay.

sentences.zh: 武、蕃得書將發，於是以朱宇為司隸校尉，劉祐為河南尹，虞祁為洛陽令。

translations.literal: When Wu and Fan obtained the letter they were about to act; thereupon they made Zhu Yu metropolitan commandant, Liu You governor of Henan, Yu Qi magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: With that letter in hand, Dou Wu and Chen Fan prepared to move: they named Zhu Yu metropolitan commandant, Liu You governor of Henan, and Yu Qi magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 武乃奏免黃門令魏彪，以所親小黃門山冰代之。

translations.literal: Wu then memorialized to dismiss yellow gate commandant Wei Biao, and in his place substituted the lesser yellow gate Shan Bing whom he trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu had the Yellow Gate commandant Wei Biao removed and replaced him with his own man, the junior eunuch Shan Bing.

sentences.zh: 使冰奏素狡猾尤無狀者長樂尚書鄭駱，送北寺獄。

translations.literal: He made Bing memorialize the Changle secretary Zheng Luo, who was by nature especially cunning and without form, and sent him to the North Prison.
translations.idiomatic: He had Shan Bing impeach Zheng Luo, secretary at Changle Palace, as the worst of the slippery eunuchs, and Zheng was packed off to the North Prison.

sentences.zh: 蕃謂武曰：「此曹子便當收殺，何復考為！

translations.literal: Fan said to Wu: "This crowd ought straightway be seized and killed; what again interrogate for!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan told Dou Wu, "Arrest those wretches and behead them; why bother with a trial?"

sentences.zh: 」武不從，令冰與尹勳、侍御史祝瑨雜考駱，辭連及曹節、王甫。

translations.literal: " Wu did not follow; he ordered Bing together with Yin Xun, attendant censor Zhu Jin, jointly to examine Luo; in his confession it connected and reached Cao Jie, Wang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu disagreed and had Shan Bing, Yin Xun, and the attendant censor Zhu Jin question Zheng Luo until his testimony implicated Cao Jie and Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 勳、冰即奏收節等，使劉瑜內奏。

translations.literal: Xun and Bing immediately memorialized to seize Jie and others, and ordered Liu Yu to memorialize within.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xun and Shan Bing memorialized for warrants against Cao Jie and his party, while Liu Yu carried the plea inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 時武出宿歸府，典中書者先以告長樂五官史朱瑀。

translations.literal: At the time Wu had gone out to lodge and returned to his residence; the one who managed the secretariat documents first used it to inform the Changle clerk of the five offices Zhu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu had spent the night at home; a clerk with access to the draft memorial tipped off Zhu Yu, the record-keeper of Changle Palace.

sentences.zh: 瑀盜發武奏，罵曰：「中官放縱者，自可誅耳。

translations.literal: Yu secretly opened Wu's memorial and cursed, saying: "Among eunuchs the unrestrained ones, naturally can be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yu stole a look at Dou Wu's memorial and swore, "If some eunuchs deserve death, kill those few."

sentences.zh: 我曹何罪，而當盡見族滅？

translations.literal: What crime have we, that we should entirely be seen exterminated by clan?
translations.idiomatic: What have the rest of us done to earn wholesale slaughter?"

sentences.zh: 」因大呼曰：「陳蕃、竇武奏白太后廢帝，為大逆！

translations.literal: " Thereupon he greatly shouted, saying: "Chen Fan and Dou Wu memorialized reporting to the empress dowager to depose the emperor; it is great treason!
translations.idiomatic: He then shouted, "Chen Fan and Dou Wu have asked the empress dowager to depose the emperor—that is treason of the highest order!"

sentences.zh: 」乃夜召素所親壯健者長樂從官史共普、張亮等十七人，喢血共盟誅武等。

translations.literal: " Then in the night he summoned seventeen men such as the Changle attendant clerk Gong Pu and Zhang Liang, whom he had long been intimate with as strong and robust; they bit blood and jointly covenanted to execute Wu and others.
translations.idiomatic: That night he rounded up seventeen trusted bravoes from Changle, among them Gong Pu and Zhang Liang, and they cut their palms and swore to kill Dou Wu and his allies.

sentences.zh: 曹節聞之，驚起，白帝曰：「外閒切切，請出御德陽前殿。

translations.literal: When Cao Jie heard it, he startled and rose, reported to the emperor, saying: "Outside there is urgent urgency; I request to go out and take the Deyang front hall.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jie heard the alarm, roused the boy emperor, and said, "Trouble is brewing outside; come with us to the front hall of Deyang Palace."

sentences.zh: 」令帝拔劍踊躍，使乳母趙嬈等擁衛左右，取棨信，閉諸禁門。

translations.literal: " He ordered the emperor to draw his sword and leap; he caused the wet nurse Zhao Rao and others to embrace and guard left and right, took tallies and credentials, and closed the various forbidden gates.
translations.idiomatic: He had the emperor brandish a sword and bustle along while Zhao Rao the wet nurse and others hemmed him in; they seized the palace tallies, sealed every inner gate, and took control.

sentences.zh: 召尚書官屬，脅以白刃，使作詔板。

translations.literal: He summoned the secretariat officials and subordinates, threatened them with bare blades, and made them compose edict boards.
translations.idiomatic: They herded the secretariat staff in at sword point and forced them to draft edicts on wooden slips.

sentences.zh: 拜王甫為黃門令，持節至北寺獄收尹勳、山冰。

translations.literal: He appointed Wang Fu yellow gate commandant, bearing credentials to the North Prison to seize Yin Xun, Shan Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu was named Yellow Gate commandant and sent with imperial credentials to the North Prison to arrest Yin Xun and Shan Bing.

sentences.zh: 冰疑，不受詔，甫格殺之。

translations.literal: Bing doubted, did not accept the edict; Fu struck and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Bing refused the order as spurious; Wang Fu cut him down on the spot.

sentences.zh: 遂害勳，出鄭駱。

translations.literal: Thereupon they harmed Xun, released Zheng Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xun was killed and Zheng Luo freed.

sentences.zh: 還共劫太后，奪璽書。

translations.literal: Returning together they coerced the empress dowager and seized the seal documents.
translations.idiomatic: They rushed back, seized the empress dowager, and wrested the imperial seals from her.

sentences.zh: 令中謁者守南宮，閉門，絕複道。

translations.literal: They ordered palace ushers to guard the Southern Palace, close gates, and cut off the covered passages.
translations.idiomatic: Palace ushers were posted in the Southern Palace; its gates were shut and the elevated walkways that linked the palaces were blocked.

sentences.zh: 使鄭駱等持節，及侍御史、謁者捕收武等。

translations.literal: They caused Zheng Luo and others to bear credentials, together with attendant censors and ushers, to seize and arrest Wu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Luo and others, credentials in hand, led attendant censors and ushers to arrest Dou Wu and his party.

sentences.zh: 武不受詔，馳入步兵營，與紹共射殺使者。

translations.literal: Wu did not accept the edict; he galloped into the foot-soldier camp, and together with Shao jointly shot and killed the messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu rejected the edict as forged, galloped to the footsoldiers' camp, and with Dou Shao shot the envoys dead.

sentences.zh: 召會北軍五校士數千人屯都亭下，令軍士曰：「黃門常侍反，盡力者封侯重賞。

translations.literal: He summoned and assembled several thousand soldiers of the five northern army camps and encamped them beneath the capital pavilion; he ordered the soldiers, saying: "The yellow gates and regular attendants rebel; those who exert strength will be enfeoffed marquis with heavy rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied several thousand men from the five northern legions at the capital guard post and told them, "The eunuchs have risen in revolt; whoever fights hardest will be enfeoffed and richly rewarded."

sentences.zh: 」詔以少府周靖行車騎將軍，加節，與護匈奴中郎將張奐率五營士討武。

translations.literal: " An edict appointed Zhou Jing of the lesser treasury acting chariot and cavalry general, added credentials, and together with the protector of the Xiongnu colonel Zhang Huan led five camp soldiers to attack Wu.
translations.idiomatic: A forged edict named Zhou Jing of the lesser treasury acting chariot-and-cavalry general, gave him the baton of command, and ordered him and the Xiongnu colonel Zhang Huan to lead the five camps against Dou Wu.

sentences.zh: 夜漏盡，王甫將虎賁、羽林、廄騶、都候、劍戟士，合千餘人，出屯朱雀掖門，與奐等合。

translations.literal: When the night clepsydra was exhausted, Wang Fu led tiger guard, feathered forest, stable grooms, capital guards, sword and halberd soldiers, together more than a thousand men, went out and encamped at the Vermilion Bird side gate, and joined with Huan and others.
translations.idiomatic: At cockcrow Wang Fu marched more than a thousand tiger guards, Feathered Forest troopers, stable grooms, capital patrols, and halberdiers to the Vermilion Bird side gate and linked up with Zhang Huan's force.

sentences.zh: 明旦悉軍闕下，與武對陳。

translations.literal: At dawn next morning they brought all their troops beneath the tower and faced off with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak they drew up their full strength below the palace towers opposite Dou Wu's men.

sentences.zh: 甫兵漸盛，使其士大呼武軍曰：「竇武反，汝皆禁兵，當宿衛宮省，何故隨反者乎？

translations.literal: Fu's soldiers gradually grew strong; he caused his soldiers greatly to shout to Wu's army, saying: "Dou Wu rebels; you all are forbidden troops, ought to night-guard the palace offices; why do you follow rebels?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu's ranks swelled; his men shouted across the lines, "Dou Wu is the traitor! You are palace guards meant to watch the emperor—why follow a rebel?"

sentences.zh: 先降有賞！

translations.literal: Those who first surrender have rewards!
translations.idiomatic: The first to come over will be rewarded!"

sentences.zh: 」營府素畏服中官，於是武軍稍稍歸甫。

translations.literal: " The camp offices always feared and submitted to inner officials; thereupon Wu's army gradually returned to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The northern camp had always feared the eunuchs, and Dou Wu's soldiers began drifting over to Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 自旦至食時，兵降略盡。

translations.literal: From dawn until mealtime, the soldiers who surrendered were nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: By midmorning his army had almost entirely melted away.

sentences.zh: 武、紹走，諸軍追圍之，皆自殺，梟首洛陽都亭。

translations.literal: Wu and Shao fled; the various armies pursued and surrounded them; they all committed suicide; their heads were displayed at the Luoyang capital pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu and Dou Shao fled, were run to ground by government troops, and killed themselves; their heads were spiked at the Luoyang guard post.

sentences.zh: 收捕宗親、賓客、姻屬，悉誅之，及劉瑜、馮述，皆夷其族。

translations.literal: They seized and arrested kinsmen, retainers, and marriage connections, all executed them, reaching Liu Yu, Feng Shu, all exterminated their clans.
translations.idiomatic: Their kin, clients, and in-laws were hunted down and executed to the last person; Liu Yu and Feng Shu were extirpated along with their entire clans.

sentences.zh: 徙武家屬日南，遷太后於雲臺。

translations.literal: They relocated Wu's family dependents to Rinan, moved the empress dowager to the Cloud Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu's family was banished to Rinan in the far south, and the empress dowager was confined on the Cloud Terrace.

sentences.zh: 當是時，凶豎得志，士大夫皆喪其氣矣。

translations.literal: At this time the evil eunuchs obtained their will, and the great officers and literati all lost their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs had won; the scholar-officials were broken in spirit.

sentences.zh: 武府掾桂陽胡騰，少師事武，獨殯斂行喪，坐以禁錮。

translations.literal: Wu’s clerk Hu Teng of Guiyang, in youth had taken Wu as teacher; alone he encoffined, gathered, and conducted mourning, and for this sat in proscription.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Teng of Guiyang, who had studied under Dou Wu in his youth and served on his staff, alone buried his patron and observed mourning for him; he was punished with lifelong disqualification from office.

sentences.zh: 武孫輔，時年二歲，逃竄得全。

translations.literal: Wu’s grandson Fu, at that time two years old, fled and hid and obtained preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wu's grandson Dou Fu, a toddler of two, was smuggled to safety.

sentences.zh: 事覺，節等捕之急。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, Jie and others urgently arrested him.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot came to light, Cao Jie and his faction hunted the child relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 胡騰及令史南陽張敞共逃輔於零陵界，詐云已死，騰以為己子，而使聘娶焉。

translations.literal: Hu Teng together with clerk Zhang Chang of Nanyang jointly fled Fu to the border of Lingling, falsely saying he had already died; Teng took him as his own son, and moreover had him betrothed and married.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Teng and the Nanyang clerk Zhang Chang spirited Dou Fu into Lingling commandery, spread word that the boy was dead, and Hu Teng raised him as his own son, even arranging a marriage for him when he came of age.

sentences.zh: 後舉桂陽孝廉。

translations.literal: Later he was recommended as filial and incorrupt of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was nominated as a filial and incorrupt candidate from Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 至建安中，荊州牧劉表聞而辟焉，以為從事，使還竇姓，以事列上。

translations.literal: When it reached the Jian'an period, Jingzhou governor Liu Biao heard and summoned him, made him a staff retainer, ordered him to return to the Dou surname, and listed the affair upward.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jian'an era, Liu Biao, governor of Jingzhou, heard the story, appointed him to his staff, had him take back the name Dou, and memorialized the whole affair to the throne.

sentences.zh: 會表卒，曹操定荊州，輔與宗人徙居於鄴，辟丞相府。

translations.literal: It happened that Biao died; Cao Cao settled Jingzhou; Fu together with clan people moved residence to Ye, and was summoned to the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao died before the matter was closed; after Cao Cao took Jingzhou, Dou Fu and his kinsmen moved to Ye, where he received an appointment in the chancellor's bureau.

sentences.zh: 從征馬超，為流矢所中死。

translations.literal: He followed on campaign against Ma Chao, was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the army against Ma Chao and was killed by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 初，武母產武而并產一蛇，送之林中。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Wu's mother gave birth to Wu she also together gave birth to one snake; she sent it into the forest.
translations.idiomatic: It is said that when Dou Wu was born, his mother also delivered a snake, which she released into the woods.

sentences.zh: 後母卒，及葬未窆，有大蛇自榛草而出，徑至喪所，以頭擊柩，涕血皆流，俯仰蛣屈，若哀泣之容，有頃而去。

translations.literal: Later when the mother died, and when burial had not yet been lowered, there was a great snake that came out from thorny grass, went straight to the mourning place, used its head to strike the coffin, tears and blood both flowed, bending up and down and coiling as if the appearance of sorrowful weeping; after a moment it departed.
translations.idiomatic: After her death, before the coffin had been lowered into the grave, a huge serpent crawled from the brush straight to the bier, butted the casket until blood and fluid streamed from its head, writhed as if weeping, then slipped away.

sentences.zh: 時人知為竇氏之祥。

translations.literal: People of the time knew it as an omen of the Dou clan.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries took it for a portent of the Dou family's strange fortune.

sentences.zh: 騰字子升。

translations.literal: Teng's courtesy name was Zisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Teng's courtesy name was Zisheng.

sentences.zh: 初，桓帝巡狩南陽，以騰為護駕從事。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Emperor Huan toured and hunted in Nanyang, he made Teng attendant for guarding the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huan toured Nanyang, he named Hu Teng an attendant for the imperial escort.

sentences.zh: 公卿貴戚車騎萬計，徵求費役，不可勝極。

translations.literal: Dukes, ministers, and noble kin, chariots and riders counted by myriads; requisitions, expenses, and corvée could not be exhausted to the limit.
translations.idiomatic: The great families descended with countless carriages and mounts; their demands for labor and supplies were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 騰上言：「天子無外，乘輿所幸，即為京師。

translations.literal: Teng submitted upward, saying: "The Son of Heaven has no outside; wherever the imperial carriage favors, that is the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Teng memorialized: "The emperor has no realm outside himself: wherever the imperial chariot rests becomes, for the moment, the capital.

sentences.zh: 臣請以荊州刺史比司隸校尉，臣自同都官從事。

translations.literal: Your subject requests to compare the Jingzhou governor to the metropolitan commandant; your subject himself compares to the capital official attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Let the governor of Jingzhou act with the authority of the metropolitan commandant, and let me serve as his capital attendant—like a metropolitan investigator."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 自是肅然，莫敢妄有干欲，騰以此顯名。

translations.literal: From this there was solemn order; none dared rashly to have intrusive desires; Teng by this became illustriously named.
translations.idiomatic: Order was restored: no one dared make arbitrary demands, and Hu Teng won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 黨錮解，官至尚書。

translations.literal: When the partisan proscription was lifted, his office reached secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After the partisan ban was lifted, he rose to secretary in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 張敞者，太尉溫之弟也。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang was the younger brother of Grand Commandant Zhang Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang was a younger brother of Grand Commandant Zhang Wen.

sentences.zh: 何進字遂高，南陽宛人也。

translations.literal: He Jin, courtesy name Suigao, was a native of Wan in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin, styled Suigao, came from Wan in Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 異母女弟選入掖庭為貴人，有寵於靈帝，拜進郎中，再遷虎賁中郎將，出為潁川太守。

translations.literal: A younger sister born of a different mother was selected into the Rear Palace and became an honored lady; she had favor with Emperor Ling. Jin was appointed gentleman of the palace, twice promoted to leader of the palace tiger guard, and sent out as governor of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: A half-sister entered the harem as an honored consort and won Emperor Ling's favor; He Jin became a gentleman attendant, rose twice to command the palace tiger guard, and was then posted as governor of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 光和二年，貴人立為皇后，徵進入，拜侍中、將作大匠、河南尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guanghe, the honored lady was established as empress; Jin was summoned in, appointed palace attendant, minister of imperial construction, and governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In 179 CE she was made empress; He Jin was recalled to court as palace attendant, minister of imperial construction, and governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 中平元年，黃巾賊張角等起，以進為大將軍，率左右羽林五營士屯都亭，修理器械，以鎮京師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongping, when the Yellow Turban bandits Zhang Jiao and others rose, Jin was made grand general; he led the left and right Feathered Forest and five camp soldiers to encamp at the capital pavilion, repaired weapons and tools, in order to pacify the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 184 CE, when Zhang Jiao's Yellow Turbans rose, He Jin was named grand general; he encamped the Feathered Forest guards and the five northern legions at the metropolitan guard post and readied arms to secure Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 張角別黨馬元義謀起洛陽，進發其姦，以功封慎侯。

translations.literal: Ma Yuanyi, a separate faction of Zhang Jiao, plotted to rise in Luoyang; Jin exposed his treachery, and for merit was enfeoffed marquis of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin uncovered a plot by Ma Yuanyi, a confederate of Zhang Jiao, to strike inside Luoyang, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shen for the deed.

sentences.zh: 四年，滎陽賊數千人群起，攻燒郡縣，殺中牟縣令，詔使進弟河南尹苗出擊之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, several thousand Xingyang bandits rose in a body, attacked and burned commanderies and counties, killed the magistrate of Zhongmou; an edict ordered Jin's younger brother He Miao, governor of Henan, to go out and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: In 187 CE thousands of Xingyang raiders torched government offices and killed the magistrate of Zhongmou; the court ordered He Jin's brother He Miao, governor of Henan, to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 苗攻破群賊，平定而還。

translations.literal: Miao broke the bandit hosts, pacified them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He Miao routed the rebels and restored calm.

sentences.zh: 詔遣使者迎於成皋，拜苗為車騎將軍，封濟陽侯。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched envoys to welcome him at Chenggao, appointed Miao chariot-and-cavalry general, and enfeoffed him marquis of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial envoys received him at Chenggao; He Miao was promoted to chariot-and-cavalry general and made Marquis of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，天下滋亂，望氣者以為京師當有大兵，兩宮流血。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the realm grew increasingly chaotic; those who read vapors thought the capital would see great armies and the two palaces would shed blood.
translations.idiomatic: In 188 CE disorder spread; court astrologers warned of great armies at the capital and bloodshed in both palaces.

sentences.zh: 大將軍司馬許涼、假司馬伍宕說進曰：「太公六韜有天子將兵事，可以威厭四方。

translations.literal: The grand general's major Xu Liang and acting major Wu Dang persuaded Jin, saying: "In the Grand Duke's Six Secret Teachings there is the Son of Heaven leading troops; by it one can awe and subdue the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: His majors Xu Liang and Wu Dang urged He Jin, citing the Grand Duke's Six Secret Teachings: if the emperor took the field in person, he would overawe the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 」進以為然，入言之於帝。

translations.literal: " Jin thought this right and entered to speak of it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin agreed and laid the proposal before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 於是乃詔進大發四方兵，講武於平樂觀下。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Jin greatly to raise troops from the four quarters and drill soldiers beneath the Pingle Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered He Jin to levy troops from across the empire and hold a grand review below the Pingle Lodge.

sentences.zh: 起大壇，上建十二重五采華蓋，高十丈，壇東北為小壇，復建九重華蓋，高九丈，列步兵，騎士數萬人，結營為陳。

translations.literal: They raised a great altar; on top was built a twelve-layer five-colored canopy, ten zhang high; northeast of the altar was a small altar, again with a nine-layer canopy, nine zhang high; they arrayed foot soldiers and mounted riders in the tens of thousands, tying camps into formation.
translations.idiomatic: They built a towering altar with a twelve-tiered, multicolored canopy, and a smaller altar with a nine-tiered canopy; tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry were drawn up in battle order.

sentences.zh: 天子親出臨軍，駐大華蓋下，進駐小華蓋下。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven personally went out to the army, halted beneath the great canopy; Jin halted beneath the small canopy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode out to review the host and took station under the great canopy while He Jin stood under the smaller one.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，帝躬擐甲介馬，稱「無上將軍」，行陳三匝而還。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, the emperor personally donned armor and barded horse, styled himself "supreme commander," circled the formation three times, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony ended, the emperor armed himself, mounted a caparisoned horse, styled himself Supreme Commander, rode three circuits through the ranks, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔使進悉領兵屯於觀下。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jin entirely to lead the troops and encamp beneath the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to keep the entire force encamped below the lodge.

sentences.zh: 是時置西園八校尉，以小黃門蹇碩為上軍校尉，虎賁中郎將袁紹為中軍校尉，屯騎都尉鮑鴻為下軍校尉，議郎曹操為典軍校尉，趙融為助軍校尉，淳于瓊為佐軍校尉，又有左右校尉。

translations.literal: At this time the eight colonels of the Western Garden were established: the lesser yellow gate Jian Shuo was senior colonel, tiger guard leader Yuan Shao was middle colonel, colonel of garrison cavalry Bao Hong was junior colonel, gentleman consultant Cao Cao was marshal colonel, Zhao Rong was assistant colonel, Chunyu Qiong was deputy colonel, and there were also left and right colonels.
translations.idiomatic: The court created eight Western Garden colonelcies: the eunuch Jian Shuo as senior colonel, Yuan Shao of the tiger guard as middle colonel, Bao Hong as junior colonel, Cao Cao as marshal colonel, with Zhao Rong and Chunyu Qiong as assistant and deputy colonels, plus left and right colonels.

sentences.zh: 帝以蹇碩壯健而有武略，特親任之，以為元帥，督司隸校尉以下，雖大將軍亦領屬焉。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Jian Shuo was strong and had military strategy, especially favored and trusted him, made him commander-in-chief, supervised from metropolitan commandant downward; even the grand general was also subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling favored Jian Shuo for his vigor and tactical sense, named him supreme commander over all forces including the metropolitan commandant, and even He Jin the grand general had to answer to him.

sentences.zh: 碩雖擅兵於中，而猶畏忌於進，乃與諸常侍共說帝遣進西擊邊章、韓遂。

translations.literal: Though Shuo monopolized troops within, he still feared and was jealous of Jin; then together with the various regular attendants he persuaded the emperor to send Jin west to attack Bian Zhang and Han Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Shuo controlled the palace armies yet feared He Jin; he and the chief eunuchs persuaded the emperor to send He Jin west against Bian Zhang and Han Sui.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，賜兵車百乘，虎賁斧鉞。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it, granted one hundred war chariots, tiger guard axes and halberds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and gave him a hundred war chariots plus the palace tiger guard's axes and halberds as emblems of command.

sentences.zh: 進陰知其謀，乃上遣袁紹東擊徐兗二州兵，須紹還，即戎事，以稽行期。

translations.literal: Jin secretly knew their plot; then he memorialized to dispatch Yuan Shao east to attack the troops of the two provinces Xu and Yan; he waited for Shao to return, then military affairs, in order to delay the date of departure.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin saw through the ruse and memorialized that Yuan Shao be sent east against forces in Xu and Yan, vowing to march west only after Yuan returned—stalling his departure.

sentences.zh: 初，何皇后生皇子辯，王貴人生皇子協。

translations.literal: In the beginning, Empress He bore the imperial son Bian; Honored Lady Wang bore the imperial son Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Empress He had borne Prince Liu Bian; Honored Lady Wang had borne Prince Liu Xie.

sentences.zh: 群臣請立太子，帝以辯輕佻無威儀，不可為人主，然皇后有寵，且進又居重權，故久不決。

translations.literal: The various ministers requested to establish the heir apparent; the emperor, because Bian was frivolous and without dignified bearing, could not be lord of men, yet the empress had favor, and moreover Jin also occupied heavy power; therefore long it was not decided.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers pressed for a crown prince; Emperor Ling thought Liu Bian too flighty to rule, yet the empress held his favor and He Jin wielded great power, so the choice dragged on unresolved.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝疾篤，屬協於蹇碩。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the emperor was critically ill and entrusted Xie to Jian Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: In 189 CE, as the emperor lay dying, he entrusted Liu Xie to Jian Shuo.

sentences.zh: 碩既受遺詔，且素輕忌於進兄弟，及帝崩，碩時在內，欲先誅進而立協。

translations.literal: Shuo had received the testamentary edict, and always lightly envied Jin and his brothers; when the emperor died, Shuo was inside and wished first to execute Jin and then establish Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Shuo held the deathbed edict and had long resented the He brothers; when the emperor died he was in the palace and meant to kill He Jin first and place Liu Xie on the throne.

sentences.zh: 及進從外入，碩司馬潘隱與進早舊，迎而目之。

translations.literal: When Jin came from outside, Shuo's major Pan Yin was long old with Jin; he welcomed him and signaled with his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: As He Jin approached from outside, Pan Yin—Jian Shuo's major but an old friend of He Jin—met him and shot him a warning look.

sentences.zh: 進驚，馳從儳道歸營，引兵入屯百郡邸，因稱疾不入。

translations.literal: Jin was alarmed; he galloped by a side path back to camp, led troops in to encamp at the hostelry of the hundred commanderies, and on that account claimed illness and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin bolted down a side lane to his camp, marched his men into the hostel where visiting officials lodged, and pleaded illness to avoid entering the palace.

sentences.zh: 碩謀不行，皇子辯乃即位，何太后臨朝，進與太傅袁隗輔政，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Shuo's plot was not carried out; the imperial son Bian then ascended the throne; Empress Dowager He faced the court; Jin together with Grand Tutor Yuan Wei assisted government and recorded secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Shuo's plot collapsed; Liu Bian succeeded as emperor; Empress Dowager He assumed the regency; He Jin and Grand Tutor Yuan Wei ran the government with authority over the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 進素知中官天下所疾，兼忿蹇碩圖己，及秉朝政，陰規誅之。

translations.literal: Jin always knew inner officials were what the realm hated; moreover he resented Jian Shuo plotting against himself; when he held court government, he secretly planned to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin knew the empire loathed the eunuchs and burned to settle scores with Jian Shuo; once in power he quietly planned the eunuch's death.

sentences.zh: 袁紹亦素有謀，因進親客張津勸之曰：「黃門常侍權重日久，又與長樂太后專通姦利，將軍宜更清選賢良，整齊天下，為國家除患。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao also long had plans; through Jin's intimate client Zhang Jin he urged him, saying: "The yellow gates and regular attendants have held heavy power for a long time, and moreover with the Dowager Empress of Changle they monopolize treacherous profit; the general ought to replace and clearly select worthies, order the realm, and remove trouble for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao, who had long nursed the same ambition, sent He Jin's confidant Zhang Jin with this counsel: the chief eunuchs had held power for years and, with the Dowager of Changle Palace, skimmed illicit gains; He Jin should purge the ranks, promote worthy men, set the realm to rights, and rid the state of this scourge.

sentences.zh: 」進然其言。

translations.literal: " Jin approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 又以袁氏累世寵貴，海內所歸，而紹素善養士，能得豪傑用，其從弟虎賁中郎將術亦尚氣俠，故並厚待之。

translations.literal: Moreover because the Yuan clan for accumulated generations had enjoyed favor and nobility, to whom the realm within the seas turned, while Shao was always good at nurturing knights and could employ heroes, and his cousin the tiger guard leader Shu also esteemed chivalrous spirit, therefore he together generously treated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan house had been honored for generations and commanded loyalty across the empire; Yuan Shao knew how to gather fighting men, and his cousin Yuan Shu, another tiger guard leader, was a man of bravado—so He Jin treated both with lavish favor.

sentences.zh: 因復博徵智謀之士龐紀、何顒、荀攸等，與同腹心。

translations.literal: Therefore he again broadly summoned men of wisdom and stratagem such as Pang Ji, He Yong, and Xun You, and with them shared innermost counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned strategists such as Pang Ji, He Yong, and Xun You and took them into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 蹇碩疑不自安，與中常侍趙忠等書曰：「大將軍兄弟秉國專朝，今與天下黨人謀誅先帝左右，埽滅我曹。

translations.literal: Jian Shuo was suspicious and not at ease; he wrote a letter to the regular attendant Zhao Zhong and others, saying: "The grand general's brothers hold the state and monopolize the court; now with the realm's partisan men they plot to execute the former emperor's attendants and sweep away our crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Jian Shuo wrote to Zhao Zhong and his fellow eunuchs: "The He brothers monopolize the court; they have joined the partisans of the realm to slaughter the late emperor's household servants and wipe us out.

sentences.zh: 但以碩典禁兵，故且沈吟。

translations.literal: Only because Shuo manages the forbidden troops, therefore for the moment I hesitate.
translations.idiomatic: Only my command of the palace troops has stayed their hand—for now.

sentences.zh: 今宜共閉上閤，急捕誅之。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting together to close the upper gate and urgently seize and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: We must seal the inner gates at once and cut them down before they move.

sentences.zh: 」中常侍郭勝，進同郡人也。

translations.literal: " The regular attendant Guo Sheng was a man of Jin's same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was the eunuch Guo Sheng, a fellow townsman of He Jin.

sentences.zh: 太后及進之貴幸，勝有力焉。

translations.literal: In the empress dowager's and Jin's noble favor, Sheng had exerted strength therein.
translations.idiomatic: He had helped the empress dowager and He Jin rise to power.

sentences.zh: 故勝親信何氏，遂共趙忠等議，不從碩計，而以其書示進。

translations.literal: Therefore Sheng trusted the He clan; then together with Zhao Zhong and others they discussed, did not follow Shuo's plan, but showed his letter to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Sheng sided with the Hes; he and Zhao Zhong rejected Jian Shuo's scheme and handed his letter to He Jin.

sentences.zh: 進乃使黃門令收碩，誅之，因領其屯兵。

translations.literal: Jin then ordered the yellow gate commandant to seize Shuo, executed him, and thereby took command of his encamped troops.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin had the Yellow Gate commandant arrest Jian Shuo, put him to death, and absorb his troops.

sentences.zh: 袁紹復說進曰：「前竇武欲誅內寵而反為所害者，以其言語漏泄，而五營百官服畏中人故也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao again persuaded Jin, saying: "The reason former Dou Wu wished to execute inner favorites but instead was harmed by them was that his words leaked, and the five camps and hundred officials submitted to and feared inner men.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao urged He Jin again: Dou Wu had fallen because word of his plot leaked and the northern legions and the bureaucracy still feared the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 今將軍既有元舅之重，而兄弟並領勁兵，部曲將吏皆英俊名士，樂盡力命，事在掌握，此天贊之時也。

translations.literal: Now the general already has the weight of the chief maternal uncle, while brothers together lead crack troops; division commanders and officers are all heroic scholars who joyfully exhaust life and orders; the matter is in the palm of the hand—this is a time when heaven aids.
translations.idiomatic: You are the emperor's uncle, your brothers command crack troops, and your officers are bold literati ready to die for you—the moment is yours; heaven itself favors you.

sentences.zh: 將軍宜一為天下除患，名垂後世。

translations.literal: The general ought once for the realm to remove trouble; your name will hang for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Strike once for the empire and your name will live in history.

sentences.zh: 雖周之申伯，何足道哉！

translations.literal: Though the Zhou's Shen Bo, what is worth speaking of!
translations.idiomatic: Even Shen Bo of Zhou would pale beside you!

sentences.zh: 今大行在前殿，將軍宜受詔領禁兵，不宜輕出入宮省。

translations.literal: Now the grand deceased lies in the front hall; the general ought to receive the edict and lead the forbidden troops; you ought not lightly go in and out of the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor lies in state in the front hall; you should take edict command of the palace guard and avoid routine comings and goings in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 」進甚然之，乃稱疾不入陪喪，又不送山陵。

translations.literal: " Jin greatly approved this; then he claimed illness, did not enter to accompany mourning, and also did not escort to the mountain tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin agreed; he stayed away from the lying-in-state on plea of illness and skipped the funeral cortège to the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 遂與紹定籌策，而以其計白太后。

translations.literal: Then he with Shao settled strategy, and with that plan reported to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yuan Shao fixed their strategy and laid it before the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后不聽，曰：「中官統領禁省，自古及今，漢家故事，不可廢也。

translations.literal: The empress dowager did not listen; she said: "Inner officials command the forbidden precincts; from ancient to present it is the Han house's story; it cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: She refused: eunuchs had commanded the inner palace from antiquity to the present; it was Han precedent and could not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 且先帝新棄天下，我奈何楚楚與士人對共事乎？

translations.literal: Moreover the former emperor has newly abandoned the realm; how can I primly face scholars and share in managing affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the late emperor had only just died—was she to stand there fussing like a scholar at council with him?

sentences.zh: 」進難違太后意，且欲誅其放縱者。

translations.literal: " Jin found it difficult to violate the empress dowager's intent, and moreover wished to execute those who were unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin could not override his sister, so he settled for executing only the worst offenders.

sentences.zh: 紹以為中官親近至尊，出入號令，今不悉廢，後必為患。

translations.literal: Shao thought inner officials were intimate with the supreme, went in and out issuing orders; if now they were not entirely abolished, later they would certainly become a scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao argued that eunuchs stood closest to the throne and issued orders in his name; unless the institution was rooted out, it would bring disaster later.

sentences.zh: 而太后母舞陽君及苗數受諸宦官賂遺，知進欲誅之。

translations.literal: But the empress dowager's mother the Lady of Wuyang and Miao repeatedly received bribe gifts from the various eunuchs and knew Jin wished to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's mother, the Lady of Wuyang, and He Miao had taken repeated bribes from the eunuchs and knew He Jin meant to kill them.

sentences.zh: 數白太后，為其障蔽。

translations.literal: Repeatedly they reported to the empress dowager and for them obstructed and screened.
translations.idiomatic: They importuned the empress dowager until she shielded the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 又言：「大將軍專殺左右，擅權以弱社稷。

translations.literal: They also said: "The grand general specializedly kills those at his side and monopolizes power to weaken the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: They whispered that the grand general was killing attendants at will and seizing power to the harm of the state.

sentences.zh: 」太后疑以為然。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager suspected and thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager began to believe them.

sentences.zh: 中官在省闥者或數十年，封侯貴寵，膠固內外。

translations.literal: Inner officials in the palace gates, some for several decades, had been enfeoffed marquises with noble favor, glued solid between inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: The chief eunuchs had served decades behind the gates, held noble titles, and had the inner and outer court bound together in their interest.

sentences.zh: 進新當重任，素敬憚之，雖外收大名而內不能斷，故事久不決。

translations.literal: Jin newly bore heavy responsibility, always respected and feared them; though outside he collected a great name, inside he could not decide; therefore the affair long went undecided.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin, new to supreme power, still feared them; he won praise in the capital yet could not bring himself to act, and the stalemate dragged on.

sentences.zh: 紹等又為畫策，多召四方猛將及諸豪傑，使並引兵向京城，以脅太后。

translations.literal: Shao and others again drew a plan: greatly summon fierce generals of the four quarters and various heroes, cause them together to lead troops toward the capital, in order to coerce the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao and his party proposed summoning regional strongmen to march on the capital and intimidate the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 進然之。

translations.literal: Jin approved it.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin agreed.

sentences.zh: 主簿陳琳入諫曰：「易稱『即鹿無虞』，諺有『掩目捕雀』。

translations.literal: Registrar Chen Lin entered and remonstrated, saying: The Changes says 'hunting deer without a forester'; the proverb has 'covering the eyes to catch sparrows'.
translations.idiomatic: His registrar Chen Lin objected: the Book of Changes warns against hunting deer without a guide, and the proverb speaks of catching sparrows blindfolded.

sentences.zh: 夫微物尚不可欺以得志，況國之大事，其可以詐立乎？

translations.literal: Humble creatures still cannot be deceived to obtain one's will; how much more a great affair of the state—can it be established by deceit?
translations.idiomatic: Small game cannot be taken by trickery; how then could the fate of the state rest on a ruse?

sentences.zh: 今將軍總皇威，握兵要，龍驤虎步，高下在心，此猶鼓洪爐燎毛髮耳。

translations.literal: Now the general gathers imperial awe, grasps the military essentials, dragon-soaring tiger-pacing, high and low in your heart—this is like drumming a great furnace to burn hair.
translations.idiomatic: You hold imperial authority and the army's heart; you stride like dragon and tiger with every advantage—using you against the eunuchs is like stoking a blast furnace to singe a hair.

sentences.zh: 夫違經合道，天人所順，而反委釋利器，更徵外助。

translations.literal: To depart from the classics yet accord with the Way is what heaven and men comply with; yet instead you relinquish the sharp weapon and again summon outside aid.
translations.idiomatic: When action accords with principle, heaven and men alike approve; yet you would lay aside a sure weapon and call in outsiders.

sentences.zh: 大兵聚會，彊者為雄，所謂倒持干戈，授人以柄，功必不成，秖為亂階。

translations.literal: When great armies gather, the strong become chieftains—what is called inverting the shield and spear and handing men the handle; the merit will certainly not be completed, it only becomes a ladder to chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Massed armies make the strongest man master—an inverted spear whose haft you hand your enemy; you would not succeed, you would only invite chaos.

sentences.zh: 」進不聽。

translations.literal: " Jin did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin would not listen.

sentences.zh: 遂西召前將軍董卓屯關中上林苑，又使府掾太山王匡東發其郡強弩，并召東郡太守橋瑁屯城皋，使武猛都尉丁原燒孟津，火照城中，皆以誅宦官為言。

translations.literal: Then he summoned west former general Dong Zhuo to encamp at Shanglin Park in Guanzhong, also ordered clerk Wang Kuang of Taishan east to dispatch his commandery's strong crossbows, together summoned East commandery governor Qiao Mao to encamp at Chenggao, ordered fierce colonel Ding Yuan to burn Meng Ford; fire illuminated the city—all with executing the eunuchs as their stated aim.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Dong Zhuo from the west to camp at Shanglin Park, ordered his clerk Wang Kuang of Taishan to levy crossbowmen, called Qiao Mao, governor of Dong commandery, to Chenggao, and sent the fierce colonel Ding Yuan to set fires at Meng Ford so that the glow lit Luoyang—every move announced as a move against the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 太后猶不從。

translations.literal: The empress dowager still did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager still refused.

sentences.zh: 苗謂進曰：「始共從南陽來，俱以貧賤，依省內以致貴富。

translations.literal: Miao said to Jin: At first together we came from Nanyang, all because poor and lowly, relied on the inner precinct to achieve noble wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He Miao told his brother: they had come up from Nanyang as poor men and leaned on the inner court to win rank and riches.

sentences.zh: 國家之事，亦何容易！

translations.literal: Affairs of altars and grain—how easy are they!
translations.idiomatic: Statecraft is never simple!

sentences.zh: 覆水不可收。

translations.literal: Spilled water cannot be gathered back.
translations.idiomatic: Spilled water cannot be scooped back into the bowl.

sentences.zh: 宜深思之，且與省內和也。

translations.literal: You ought deeply to ponder this, and moreover harmonize with the inner precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Think hard on that, and make peace with the palace.

sentences.zh: 」進意更狐疑。

translations.literal: " Jin's intent became more fox-suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin grew only more hesitant.

sentences.zh: 紹懼進變計，乃脅之曰：「交搆已成，形埶已露，事留變生，將軍復欲何待，而不早決之乎？

translations.literal: Shao feared Jin would change plans; then he threatened him, saying: "The cross-structure is already completed, the situation already exposed; if the affair is delayed change will arise—what again does the general wait for, and not early decide it?
translations.idiomatic: Fearing He Jin would waver, Yuan Shao pressed him: the snare was set and their purpose known; delay bred treachery—what was he waiting for?

sentences.zh: 」進於是以紹為司隸校尉，假節，專命擊斷；

translations.literal: " Jin thereupon appointed Shao metropolitan commandant, granted credentials, exclusive authority to strike and judge;
translations.idiomatic: He Jin then named Yuan Shao metropolitan commandant, gave him the baton, and authorized summary executions;

sentences.zh: 從事中郎王允為河南尹。

translations.literal: staff supervisor Wang Yun was governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed Wang Yun, his staff supervisor, governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 紹使洛陽方略武吏司察宦者，而促董卓等使馳驛上，欲進兵平樂觀。

translations.literal: Shao ordered Luoyang scouts and martial clerks to investigate the eunuchs, and urged Dong Zhuo and others to hurry by relay toward the capital, wishing to advance troops to the Pingle Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao set Luoyang's investigators on the eunuchs and prodded Dong Zhuo and the rest to race toward the capital, intent on marching to the Pingle Lodge.

sentences.zh: 太后乃恐，悉罷中常侍小黃門，使還里舍，唯留進素所私人，以守省中。

translations.literal: The empress dowager then feared; she entirely dismissed regular attendants and lesser yellow gates, ordered them to return to neighborhood houses, only kept Jin's long-time private men to guard the inner precinct.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager panicked and dismissed every chief eunuch and junior Yellow Gate attendant to their suburban quarters, leaving only He Jin's personal agents inside.

sentences.zh: 諸常侍小黃門皆詣進謝罪，唯所措置。

translations.literal: All regular attendants and lesser yellow gates came to Jin to apologize for their faults, leaving whatever disposition.
translations.idiomatic: The dismissed eunuchs flocked to He Jin to beg pardon and await his orders.

sentences.zh: 進謂曰：「天下匈匈，正患諸君耳。

translations.literal: Jin said to them: The realm is in an uproar; precisely you gentlemen are the worry.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin told them the realm was in turmoil, and they were the trouble.

sentences.zh: 今董卓垂至，諸君何不早各就國？

translations.literal: Now Dong Zhuo is about to arrive; why do you gentlemen not early each return to your feudatories?
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo was almost there—why not retire at once to their estates?

sentences.zh: 」袁紹勸進便於此決之，至于再三。

translations.literal: " Yuan Shao urged Jin to decide at this point, reaching thrice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao begged him to settle accounts then and there—again and again.

sentences.zh: 進不許。

translations.literal: Jin did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin refused.

sentences.zh: 紹又為書告諸州郡，詐宣進意，使捕案中官親屬。

translations.literal: Shao again wrote letters announcing to the various provinces and commanderies, falsely declaring Jin's intent, ordering arrest and investigation of inner officials' kin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao forged orders in He Jin's name to the provinces, commanding the arrest of eunuchs' relatives.

sentences.zh: 進謀積日，頗泄，中官懼而思變。

translations.literal: Jin's plot accumulated over days and somewhat leaked; inner officials feared and thought of turning the tables.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin's plans leaked day by day, and the eunuchs grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 張讓子婦，太后之妹也。

translations.literal: Zhang Rang's daughter-in-law was the empress dowager's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang's daughter-in-law was the empress dowager's own sister.

sentences.zh: 讓向子婦叩頭曰：「老臣得罪，當與新婦俱歸私門。

translations.literal: Rang knocked his head toward his daughter-in-law and said: This old minister has offended; I ought together with the new wife to return to the private gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang kowtowed to her and said he had earned her displeasure and should go home with his daughter-in-law.

sentences.zh: 惟受恩累世，今當遠離宮殿，情懷戀戀，願復一入直，得暫奉望太后、陛下顏色，然後退就溝壑，死不恨矣。

translations.literal: Only I have received favor for accumulated generations; now about to far leave the palace halls, my feelings linger; I wish again once to enter on duty, obtain briefly to attend and gaze upon the empress dowager's and Your Majesty's countenance, then retire to ditches and gullies; in death I will have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: They had served many reigns; leaving the palace grieved them. They begged one last turn of duty to look upon the empress dowager and His Majesty, then they would crawl into their graves content.

sentences.zh: 」子婦言於舞陽君，入白太后，乃詔諸常侍皆復入直。

translations.literal: " The daughter-in-law spoke to the Lady of Wuyang, entered and reported to the empress dowager; then an edict ordered all regular attendants again to enter on duty.
translations.idiomatic: She relayed the plea to the Lady of Wuyang, who told the empress dowager; an edict recalled the chief eunuchs to their posts.

sentences.zh: 八月，進入長樂白太后，請盡誅諸常侍以下，選三署郎入守宦官廬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Jin entered Changle, reported to the empress dowager, requested entirely to execute all regular attendants and below, and select gentlemen of the three offices to enter and guard the eunuchs' lodges.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month He Jin went to Changle Palace and asked the empress dowager to execute every chief eunuch down the line and replace them with gentlemen cadets from the three offices.

sentences.zh: 諸宦官相謂曰：「大將軍稱疾不臨喪，不送葬，今欻入省，此意何為？

translations.literal: The various eunuchs said to each other: The grand general claimed illness, did not attend mourning, did not escort the burial; now suddenly he enters the inner precinct—what is this intent?
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs whispered among themselves: the grand general had shunned the lying-in-state and the funeral; now he burst into the inner court—what did he mean?

sentences.zh: 竇氏事竟復起邪？

translations.literal: Is the Dou clan affair after all rising again?
translations.idiomatic: Was the Dou Wu affair to be replayed?

sentences.zh: 」又張讓等使人潛聽，具聞其語，乃率常侍段珪、畢嵐等數十人，持兵竊自側闥入，伏省中。

translations.literal: " Moreover Zhang Rang and others sent people secretly to listen; they fully heard these words; then they led several tens of men including regular attendants Duan Gui and Bi Lan, held weapons, secretly entered from a side door, and lay in ambush in the inner precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang had listeners who caught every word; he and Duan Gui, Bi Lan, and dozens of others armed themselves, slipped in through a side door, and hid inside.

sentences.zh: 及進出，因詐以太后詔召進。

translations.literal: When Jin came out, they then falsely used the empress dowager's edict to summon Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When He Jin emerged, they forged a summons in the empress dowager's name.

sentences.zh: 入坐省闥，讓等詰進曰：「天下憒憒，亦非獨我曹罪也。

translations.literal: He entered and sat in the inner gate; Rang and others questioned Jin, saying: The realm is restless; it is also not solely our crowd's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the gate Zhang Rang confronted him: the empire seethed, and they were not the only guilty ones.

sentences.zh: 先帝嘗與太后不快，幾至成敗，我曹涕泣救解，各出家財千萬為禮，和悅上意，但欲託卿門戶耳。

translations.literal: The former emperor once was displeased with the empress dowager, nearly reached success or ruin; our crowd wept tears and rescued and resolved it, each brought out family wealth in the millions as gifts, harmoniously pleased the superior's intent—only wishing to entrust ourselves to your gateway.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor once quarreled with the empress dowager to the brink of disaster; we wept and poured out our private fortunes—millions in gifts—to smooth his temper and win your family's favor.

sentences.zh: 今乃欲滅我曹種族，不亦太甚乎？

translations.literal: Now you then wish to extinguish our crowd's clans—is it not too excessive?
translations.idiomatic: Now he would wipe out their houses root and branch—was that not too much?

sentences.zh: 卿言省內穢濁，公卿以下忠清者為誰？

translations.literal: You say the inner precinct is filthy and turbid—below the dukes and ministers, who is loyal and pure?
translations.idiomatic: He called the inner court corrupt—which of the high ministers below him was spotlessly loyal?

sentences.zh: 」於是尚方監渠穆拔劍斬進於嘉德殿前。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Shangfang supervisor Qu Mu drew his sword and beheaded Jin before the Hall of Virtuous Grace.
translations.idiomatic: At that Qu Mu, director of the imperial workshops, drew his sword and cut He Jin down before the Hall of Virtuous Grace.

sentences.zh: 讓、珪等為詔，以故太尉樊陵為司隸校尉，少府許相為河南尹。

translations.literal: Rang, Gui, and others forged an edict, appointing former grand commandant Fan Ling metropolitan commandant and lesser treasury Xu Xiang governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang and Duan Gui forged edicts naming Fan Ling, the former grand commandant, metropolitan commandant and Xu Xiang of the lesser treasury governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 尚書得詔板，疑之，曰：「請大將軍出共議。

translations.literal: The secretariat obtained the edict board, doubted it, and said: We request the grand general to come out and jointly deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat received the forged slip and balked: they asked the grand general to step out and discuss it with them in person.

sentences.zh: 」中黃門以進頭擲與尚書，曰：「何進謀反，已伏誅矣。」

translations.literal: A middle yellow gate threw Jin's head to the secretariat, saying: He Jin plotted rebellion; he has already been executed.
translations.idiomatic: A palace eunuch flung He Jin's head onto their desks and said, He Jin had risen in rebellion and had already been put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 進部曲將吳匡、張璋，素所親幸，在外聞進被害，欲將兵入宮，宮閤閉。

translations.literal: Jin's division commanders Wu Kuang and Zhang Zhang, whom he had long favored, were outside; when they heard Jin had been harmed, they wished to lead troops into the palace; the palace gates were closed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kuang and Zhang Zhang, division commanders whom He Jin had favored, were outside the walls; when they learned he had been murdered they tried to force the palace gates, but the doors were barred.

sentences.zh: 袁術與匡共斫攻之，中黃門持兵守閤。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu together with Kuang jointly hacked and attacked them; middle yellow gates held weapons and guarded the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu joined Wu Kuang in hewing at the gates while eunuch guards held the line with arms.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，術因燒南宮九龍門及東西宮，欲以脅出讓等。

translations.literal: It happened that the sun set; Shu thereupon burned the Southern Palace's Nine Dragon Gate and the east and west palaces, wishing thereby to coerce Rang and others to come out.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Yuan Shu set fire to the Nine Dragon Gate of the Southern Palace and to the eastern and western annexes, hoping to smoke Zhang Rang and his party out.

sentences.zh: 讓等入白太后，言大將軍兵反，燒宮，攻尚書闥，因將太后、天子及陳留王，又劫省內官屬，從複道走北宮。

translations.literal: Rang and others entered and reported to the empress dowager, saying the grand general's troops had rebelled, burned the palace, attacked the secretariat gate; then they led the empress dowager, the Son of Heaven, and the king of Chenliu, moreover coerced inner precinct officials and subordinates, and fled by the covered passage to the Northern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang and his confederates burst in on the empress dowager with a tale that He Jin's men had mutinied, torched the palace, and stormed the secretariat; they then seized the empress dowager, the emperor, and the Prince of Chenliu, rounded up palace staff, and fled along the elevated walk to the Northern Palace.

sentences.zh: 尚書盧植執戈於閣道窗下，仰數段珪。

translations.literal: Secretary Lu Zhi grasped a halberd beneath the gallery window and looked up to rebuke Duan Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi of the secretariat stood under the gallery with a halberd and shouted up at Duan Gui.

sentences.zh: 段珪等懼，乃釋太后。

translations.literal: Duan Gui and others feared; then they released the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Gui and the others lost their nerve and let the empress dowager go.

sentences.zh: 太后投閣得免。

translations.literal: The empress dowager threw herself from the tower and obtained escape.
translations.idiomatic: She leapt from the gallery and escaped.

sentences.zh: 袁紹與叔父隗矯詔召樊陵、許相，斬之。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao together with his uncle Wei forged an edict summoning Fan Ling and Xu Xiang and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao and his uncle Yuan Wei forged orders to lure Fan Ling and Xu Xiang in and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 苗、紹乃引兵屯朱雀闕下，捕得趙忠等，斬之。

translations.literal: Miao and Shao then led troops to encamp beneath the Vermilion Bird tower gate, seized Zhao Zhong and others, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: He Miao and Yuan Shao marched to the Vermilion Bird gate, seized Zhao Zhong and his clique, and put them to the sword.

sentences.zh: 吳匡等素怨苗不與進同心，而又疑其與宦官同謀，乃令軍中曰：「殺大將軍者即車騎也，士吏能為報讎乎？

translations.literal: Wu Kuang and others always resented Miao for not being of one mind with Jin, and moreover suspected him of plotting together with the eunuchs; then they ordered the army, saying: The one who killed the grand general is precisely the chariot-and-cavalry commander; can officers and soldiers avenge the wrong?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kuang had long resented He Miao for siding against his brother and suspected him of colluding with the eunuchs; he harangued the troops, The chariot-and-cavalry general killed the grand general—will you avenge him?

sentences.zh: 」進素有仁恩，士卒皆流涕曰：「願致死！

translations.literal: Jin always had benevolent grace; the soldiers all wept tears and said: We wish to exhaust death!
translations.idiomatic: He Jin had always treated his men kindly; they wept and swore they would die for him.

sentences.zh: 」匡遂引兵與董卓弟奉車都尉旻攻殺苗，棄其屍於苑中。

translations.literal: Kuang then led troops together with Dong Zhuo's younger brother carriage attendant colonel Min, attacked and killed Miao, and cast his corpse in the park.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kuang then joined Dong Min, Dong Zhuo's younger brother and carriage attendant colonel, stormed He Miao's position, killed him, and dumped the body in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 紹遂閉北宮門，勒兵捕宦者，無少長皆殺之。

translations.literal: Shao then closed the Northern Palace gate, constrained troops to seize eunuchs, without regard to young or old all killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sealed the Northern Palace, sent soldiers hunting eunuchs, and slaughtered every one they found, young or old.

sentences.zh: 或有無須而誤死者，至自發露然後得免者二千餘人。

translations.literal: Some who had no whiskers died by mistake; those who reached exposing themselves by shaving then obtained release were more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Some men without beards were killed by mistake; more than two thousand had to strip and prove they were not eunuchs to survive.

sentences.zh: 紹因進兵排宮，或上端門屋，以攻省內。

translations.literal: Shao thereupon advanced troops and forced the palace; some ascended the roof of the Duan Gate to attack the inner precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao drove his men into the palace compounds; some climbed onto the roof of the Duan Gate to shoot down into the inner court.

sentences.zh: 張讓、段珪等困迫，遂將帝與陳留王數十人步出穀門，奔小平津。

translations.literal: Zhang Rang, Duan Gui, and others were hard pressed; then they led the emperor and the king of Chenliu with several tens of men on foot out the Grain Gate and fled to Little Ping Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Zhang Rang and Duan Gui fled on foot through the Grain Gate toward Little Ping Ford with the emperor, the Prince of Chenliu, and a few dozen followers.

sentences.zh: 公卿並出平樂觀，無得從者，唯尚書盧植夜馳河上，王允遣河南中部掾閔貢隨植後。

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers together went out to the Pingle Lodge; none could follow; only Secretary Lu Zhi galloped by night to the river; Wang Yun dispatched Henan middle clerk Min Gong to follow after Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers had all gone to the Pingle Lodge and had no escort for the emperor; only Lu Zhi of the secretariat rode through the night toward the river, and Wang Yun sent Min Gong, a clerk of Henan, on his heels.

sentences.zh: 貢至，手劍斬數人，餘皆投河而死。

translations.literal: When Gong arrived, he personally with sword beheaded several men; the rest all threw themselves in the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: Min Gong cut down several eunuchs with his own blade; the rest threw themselves into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 明日，公卿百官乃奉迎天子還宮，以貢為郎中，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: The next day, dukes, ministers, and the hundred officials then respectfully welcomed the Son of Heaven back to the palace; they appointed Gong gentleman of the palace and enfeoffed him marquis of the capital pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The following day the court escorted the emperor home, named Min Gong a gentleman attendant, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of the capital guard post.

sentences.zh: 董卓遂廢帝，又迫殺太后，殺舞陽君，何氏遂亡，而漢室亦自此敗亂。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo thereupon deposed the emperor, moreover forced and killed the empress dowager, killed the Lady of Wuyang; the He clan thereupon perished, and the Han house also from this was defeated and thrown into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo then deposed the emperor, forced the empress dowager to her death, executed the Lady of Wuyang, and wiped out the He family—after which the house of Han slid into ruin.

sentences.zh: 論曰：竇武、何進藉元舅之資，據輔政之權，內倚太后臨朝之威，外迎群英乘風之埶，卒而事敗閹豎，身死功穨，為世所悲，豈智不足而權有餘乎？

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Dou Wu and He Jin relied on the chief maternal uncle's resources, grasped the power of assisting government, inwardly leaned on the empress dowager's awe in facing the court, outwardly welcomed the host of heroes riding the wind's momentum; in the end affairs failed to the palace slaves, they died and merit collapsed, pitied by the age—was it that wisdom was insufficient while power was surplus?
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Dou Wu and He Jin held the authority of maternal uncles to the throne, commanded the regency, had the empress dowager's prestige behind them, and rallied the finest men of the age—yet both fell to eunuchs and died with their cause in ruins, objects of pity ever since. Was it too little wit and too much power?

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「天之廢商久矣，君將興之。

translations.literal: The tradition says: Heaven's abandoning Shang has been long; you, lord, will raise it.
translations.idiomatic: The tradition runs: Heaven has long since cast off Shang; you, my lord, mean to restore it.

sentences.zh: 」斯宋襄公所以敗於泓也。

translations.literal: This is why Duke Xiang of Song was defeated at Hong.
translations.idiomatic: That was the spirit in which Duke Xiang of Song met defeat at Hong.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：武生蛇祥，進自屠羊。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Wu bore the snake omen; Jin came from slaughtering sheep.
translations.idiomatic: The verse says: Dou Wu was born under a serpent's portent; He Jin rose from a butcher's stall.

sentences.zh: 惟女惟弟，來儀紫房。

translations.literal: Only the daughter, only the younger brother, came in ritual display to the purple chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Sister and brother brought their line into the purple halls of power.

sentences.zh: 上惛下嬖，人靈動怨。

translations.literal: Above benighted, below favored; men and spirits stirred with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler grew dim while favorites below ran wild; men and gods alike stirred with resentment.

sentences.zh: 將糾邪慝，以合人願。

translations.literal: They would rectify evil and treachery, in order to accord with men's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to purge wickedness and answer the people's prayer.

sentences.zh: 道之屈矣，代離凶困。

translations.literal: The Way was bent; in their stead they met fierce hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The Way turned against them; their house instead met disaster and ruin.
